text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund said it expected foreign investments in Egypt to reach $2.1 billion in the financial year 1996/7, an increase of 254 percent over last year. This includes direct investment of about $800 million, $200 million more than last year, and portfolio investment of $1.3 billion, compared with $50 million last financial year. IMF representative Arvind Subramanian said the investment rate would rise to 18 percent of GDP, one percentage point up on last year, while the savings rate would be 17 percent, the same as last financial year.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the government is now studying the possibility of exempting capital goods for the South Valley Development Project from sales tax. It has been decided to exempt them from other taxes for 20 years.

- Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, former chairman of the state's Holding Company for Engineering Industries, has been charged with illegal gain and again remanded in custody. Investigators found that Habbak illegally amassed a personal fortune of more than $24 million.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the fabric of national unity was an invincible bastion against any attempts to damage it. He also gave orders that the families of the dead in the Abu Qurqas church incident should receive 3,000 pounds ($880) each.
- Electricity Minister Maher Abaza said electricity prices would not go up when the private sector builds power stations.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said that Iran had been playing a conspiratorial role against Egypt through an Iranian embassy abroad in support of the terrorist organisation (the Gama'a al-Islamiya). He also said that the Sudanese government continues to shelter, support and train members of the organisation. He said Gama'a cells had been found in a European country and that Gama'a leaders in another European country intended to direct terrorist operations inside Egypt.

- Egypt and 11 Arab and African states have submitted a proposal to reconsider the sanctions imposed on Libya because of the Lockerbie affair at the next U.N. Security Council meeting, based on the Libyan proposal to let the accused face trial in The Hague.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Israelis who support Jewish settlements are the ones who need the education about which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken.
- The Supreme State Security Court in Giza sentenced three people to 15 years' hard labour, six to 10 years' hard labour and three to three years' hard labour for stealing antiquities.

- Official talks between President Hosni Mubarak and King Juan Carlos of Spain start tomorrow. They will talk about the peace process, regional and international developments and bilateral relations. In the evening Mubarak will host a banquet in honour of the king and queen.
